prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1440; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort at scene. Police report requested. Photos of both vehicles on file.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirms no attorney retained and states they prefer to handle the claim directly. Reports back strain, worse in the mornings, and has been seen once at an urgent care clinic. Requested the clinic records and a signed authorization form.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos of rear bumper damage on claimant vehicle and mid-level impact damage on insured vehicle. Estimate from the body shop is pending. Noted claimant's statement that the other driver admitted fault at the scene, which is consistent with the police report narrative.

Entry 4: Received urgent care records. Diagnosis is lumbar strain with muscle spasm, prescribed rest, over-the-counter anti-inflammatories, and a follow-up if symptoms persist. No imaging performed. Advised claimant of their right to seek medical follow-up and to keep receipts for all out-of-pocket expenses.

Entry 5: Claimant called to ask about the status of the claim and whether a settlement offer is coming. Explained that the file is still under evaluation pending final medical follow-up and repair estimate. Set a diary reminder to check in again in two weeks and to request a physical therapy update if one is scheduled.
